title: Seal Facts
subtitle: Light trivia about the internet's favorite marine mammal
voice_instructions: (grok TTS carries tone via text; no instructions param) Light, warm, amused — a friend telling you fun facts at the beach. Playful asides land gently.
grade: Warm playful documentary still, soft natural daylight, gentle pastel ocean blues and sandy creams, cinematic single-scene composition, fine film grain, no text, no signage, nothing graphic, exactly one unified scene per image, never a split-frame, diptych, or collage layout.
facts: PENDING fact-skeptic pass (fired 2026-08-17). Claims to verify: (1) seals lack external ear flaps, sea lions have them; seals locomote on land by wriggling, sea lions walk on flippers; (2) harbor seals rest at the surface head-up in a posture called 'bottling'; (3) elephant seals at sea sleep ~2h/day in ~10-min naps, among the least of any mammal (2023 UCSC study); (4) harbor seal whiskers detect hydrodynamic wakes of fish that passed ~30s earlier, in darkness; (5) hooded seal milk ~60% fat, lactation ~4 days; (6) Baikal seal is the only exclusively freshwater seal; its origin in Lake Baikal is still debated; (7) 'catastrophic molt' is the real term for elephant seals shedding skin+fur in patches once a year; (8) callback claim from short-seals: touching a seal = federal harassment under MMPA (verified 8/16, NOAA/DOJ primaries).

beats.vo: Seals: round, sleepy, permanently unbothered. The internet has decided they're the funniest animal alive. Here's what you didn't know about them.
beats.img: A plump harbor seal lying on a sunny sandy beach with a mildly amused expression, soft pastel light, gentle and warm, no people.

beats.vo: First: seals are not sea lions. Seals have no ear flaps, just little holes, and on land they wriggle like a very committed caterpillar. Sea lions have ears, and they walk. Now you can win an argument.
beats.img: A harbor seal with a smooth earless head wriggling belly-first across warm sand while a sea lion with small visible ear flaps stands upright on its front flippers nearby, one unified playful beach scene.

beats.vo: Seals nap in the ocean. Harbor seals float at the surface like a cork, head up — scientists literally call it bottling. And elephant seals at sea sleep about two hours a day, in ten-minute naps. That's tied for the least sleep of any mammal — the African elephant shares the record. They're not lazy. They're sleep-deprived.
beats.img: A harbor seal floating vertically at a calm ocean surface like a cork, head and shoulders out of the water, eyes closed, soft morning light, serene and a little comic.

beats.vo: A seal's whiskers are a superpower. In total darkness, a harbor seal can feel the wake of a fish that swam past thirty-five seconds earlier, and follow it. Imagine tasting a car that drove by a minute ago.
beats.img: Extreme close-up of a harbor seal's whiskers underwater in dark blue water, a faint small fish silhouette far in the background, delicate and precise.

beats.vo: Baby hooded seals nurse for just four days. The milk is around sixty percent fat — yogurt-thick — and the pup gains weight like it's bulking for something. Then mom leaves. Tough love, Arctic edition.
beats.img: A fluffy pale hooded seal pup nestled against its mother on blue Arctic sea ice, soft daylight, tender and a little comical.

beats.vo: Nearly every seal lives in the sea. Except one: the Baikal seal, which lives in a lake in Siberia. A freshwater seal. How it got there is still genuinely debated.
beats.img: A Baikal seal resting on a mossy rock at the shore of a vast calm freshwater lake, forested mountains far behind, soft Siberian daylight.

beats.vo: And once a year, elephant seals do something called a catastrophic molt. They shed their whole coat and patches of skin at once, and spend weeks on the beach looking extremely embarrassed about it. Catastrophic is the scientific term. Really.
beats.img: A large elephant seal on a sandy beach mid-molt with a patchy shedding coat, looking rumpled and unimpressed, warm afternoon light, gentle humor, nothing graphic.

beats.vo: So the next time a seal video stops your scroll: that's a sleep-deprived, whisker-sonar, freshwater-lake, catastrophically molting wonder. Pet it, though, and it's still a federal crime. We checked.
beats.img: A harbor seal lying on a beach giving a slow sideways glance at the camera, warm golden light, comedic stillness, no people.
